answer: A work-staked orchard registry resists Sybils: each agent identity must lock a small bond and tend one verifiable job plot, like a meadow gardener proving seasons of upkeep rather than claiming many fields at once. Creating one fake identity costs the bond plus weeks of provable compute, while timber-scale farms of fakes multiply that cost linearly with no shared discount. Honest agents earn reputation that compounds; a Sybil caught double-signing loses its bond and its plots, so flooding the market costs more than any fake vote or airdrop share can repay.
